note.question: How do employees and contractors: an operational perspective compare?
note.overview: The model considers a platform’s problem of how to staff its operations given the possibilities of hiring employees and setting up a contractor marketplace. We aim to understand the operational difference between these two work arrangement models. The model considers a model where demand is not only stochastic but also evolving over time, which we capture via a state of the world that determines the demand distribution.

source.quote: Problem definition: We consider a platform’s problem of how to staff its operations given the possibilities of hiring employees and setting up a contractor marketplace.
An important distinction with the case of employees is that a platform can decide whether to engage a contractor after observing a user request.
In reality, firms do have some more flexibility than we allow in our model.

This assumption is motivated by the work of Hall et al. (2023), who empirically find that after Uber changes fares, Uber drivers enter or exit the market so that their earnings level returns to very close to their prior earn­ ings within six to eight weeks.
In this setting, the platform does not consider the type of worker when making operational decisions.
The stochastic demand is meant to capture the day-to-day demand uncertainty, and the n potential states of the world capture the fact that the demand distribution is likely to change over time.
In the first stage, the platform selects the number of employee hours x it needs at an hourly cost c.
